findings.title: V2 `canManage()` grants group management to callers who only hold VIEW on groups
findings.description: The no-argument `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Its sibling `canManage(GroupModel)` checks only `MANAGE`, and `canView()` is the only method where `VIEW` is a valid grant. The Javadoc says V2 `canManage()` also accepts VIEW, so this may be intentional. If it is not, a caller with only a group VIEW permission passes `requireManage()` and could create or update groups, since the no-argument check is used for realm-level group operations. Confirm the intent and check the callers of `canManage()`.

findings.title: Per-user view filter removed from `searchForUser`
findings.description: The `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` call was removed. Results now depend only on the group-membership attribute passed to the search. User-level VIEW or MANAGE permissions, which `canView(UserModel)` honours, are no longer applied to the returned stream. Confirm that the store-side filter covers every case the removed filter covered.

findings.title: `AdminRoles.ADMIN` dropped from V2 role checks
findings.description: `canView(UserModel)`, `canManage(UserModel)`, and their V2 counterparts no longer check `AdminRoles.ADMIN`. Callers holding that role lose access that the old checks granted. This may be deliberate, but it is a behaviour change that the diff does not explain.

findings.title: Removed imports could leave unresolved references
findings.description: The diff removes `java.util.Arrays` from `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java`, `ModelToRepresentation` from `GroupsResource.java`, and `java.util.function.Predicate` from `UsersResource.java`. The hunks do not show whether any remaining code in those files still uses them. Confirm that the files compile.
